questions.question_text: A property owner sells their own home without hiring an agent. Does this require a real estate license in Vermont?
distractors: Yes, all sales require a license
Only if the owner advertises online
questions.explanation: Property owners selling their own real estate are exempt from Vermont licensing (26 V.S.A. § 2211(b)). A license is required only when a person, for another and for compensation, lists, sells, buys, exchanges, negotiates, or deals in options on real estate as a continuing course of conduct.

questions.question_text: An attorney handles real estate transactions as part of administering a deceased client's estate. Must the attorney hold a real estate license?
distractors: Yes, any sale requires a license
Only if the property value exceeds $250,000
Only if the attorney collects a commission
questions.explanation: Attorneys acting in connection with estate, trust, or bankruptcy matters are exempt from Vermont real estate licensing. This exemption recognizes the attorney's existing professional regulation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following activities requires a Vermont real estate license?
questions.correct_answer: Negotiating the sale of another person's property for a fee
distractors: Leasing or renting property for an owner for a fee
questions.explanation: 26 V.S.A. § 2211(a)(4) makes listing, selling, exchanging, purchasing, or negotiating the sale of real estate for another for compensation a licensed activity. Leasing is expressly exempt under § 2211(b)(8) and Rule 2.1(c)(1) — Vermont does not license leasing or rental property management. Appraisers are separately regulated, and owners selling their own property are exempt.

questions.question_text: A court appoints a receiver to manage and sell foreclosed properties. Does this person need a real estate license?
distractors: Yes, all property sales require a license
Only if the receiver earns a commission
Only if the receiver is not an attorney
questions.explanation: Court-appointed receivers are exempt from Vermont licensing requirements. The court appointment provides oversight that substitutes for the consumer protections of licensure.

questions.question_text: A public officer conducts a tax sale of abandoned property. Is a license required?
distractors: Yes, all sales need a license
Only if the officer profits personally
Only if the sale is over $50,000
questions.explanation: Public officers performing their official duties related to real estate are exempt from Vermont licensing requirements. Tax sales conducted by government officials fall under this exemption.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum age to obtain a salesperson license in Vermont?
questions.explanation: Vermont requires salesperson applicants to be at least 18 years of age. Additional requirements include completing 40 hours of pre-license education, passing the exam, and a background check.

questions.question_text: A salesperson wants to upgrade to a broker license. What experience requirement must be met?
questions.explanation: A Vermont broker applicant must have at least 2 years of experience as a licensed salesperson, including at least 8 separate and unrelated closed transactions among buyers and sellers who bear no familial or contemporaneous business relationship to the applicant (Commission Rule 2.5(c)), plus the 40-hour broker prelicensing course.

questions.question_text: A brokerage firm opens a second location. What must be obtained from OPR for that office?
distractors: Nothing — only a business registration with the town
A separate broker license for each agent at that office
questions.explanation: The Commission issues licenses (broker, salesperson, temporary broker) and registrations (brokerage firm and branch office) — Rule 2.3. A firm that wants more than one office must register a branch office, use the same name as the main office, and designate a broker in charge who maintains their place of business there (Rule 4.1(b)).

questions.question_text: How many additional education hours must a salesperson complete to qualify for a broker license?
questions.explanation: Vermont broker applicants must complete the broker prelicensing course of at least 40 hours approved by the Commission (Rules 1.8(c) and 5.1), in addition to 2 years of salesperson experience and 8 closed transactions.

questions.question_text: An applicant has completed the 40-hour pre-license course and passed the exams. What else must be in place before a Vermont salesperson license will be issued?
questions.correct_answer: Association with a registered brokerage firm and its principal broker
distractors: A personal interview with the Commission
questions.explanation: Commission Rule 2.4 grants a salesperson license to an applicant who is at least 18, has completed the prelicensing course, passed the national and state exams within the preceding 2 years, has been employed by or become associated with a brokerage firm and that firm's principal broker, and is not precluded from licensure under 3 V.S.A. § 129a. A salesperson cannot hold an unattached license.

questions.question_text: How many hours of pre-license education does Vermont require for a salesperson license?
questions.explanation: Vermont requires 40 hours of approved pre-license education for salesperson applicants. This must be completed before sitting for the licensing examination.

questions.question_text: A newly licensed salesperson must complete post-license education. Within what timeframe?
questions.explanation: Vermont requires newly licensed salespersons to complete 8 hours of post-license education within 90 days of receiving their license.

questions.question_text: How many continuing education hours must a Vermont salesperson complete each renewal cycle?
questions.explanation: Vermont salespersons must complete 16 hours of continuing education every 2-year renewal cycle, including 4 hours of mandatory topics designated by the Commission.

questions.question_text: A Vermont broker is preparing for license renewal. How many CE hours are required per cycle?
questions.explanation: Vermont brokers must complete 24 hours of continuing education every 2-year renewal cycle, which is 8 more hours than the salesperson requirement of 16 hours.

questions.question_text: Of the 16 CE hours required for salesperson renewal, how many must cover mandatory topics?
questions.explanation: Vermont salespersons must complete 4 hours of mandatory topics as part of their 16-hour CE requirement. The remaining 12 hours may be in elective subjects.

questions.question_text: When does a Vermont real estate SALESPERSON license expire?
questions.explanation: Vermont licenses renew on a fixed biennial schedule (Rule 3.1). Salesperson licenses expire May 31 of even-numbered years; broker licenses expire March 31 of even-numbered years. Watch for that split — the two license types do not share a renewal date.

questions.question_text: What is the license renewal fee for a Vermont real estate licensee?
questions.explanation: The Vermont real estate license renewal fee is $220. Other fees include $100 for the initial application and $110 for the licensing exam.

questions.question_text: A salesperson switches to a new brokerage firm. What must be done with OPR?
questions.explanation: A principal broker or broker in charge must notify OPR in writing within 30 days of any change in the name, address, phone, or email of the firm or of any licensee associated with it, and each licensee must notify OPR within 30 days of a change in their own principal business location (Rule 3.4). No new exam or extra education is required.

questions.question_text: A Vermont salesperson's license expired two renewal cycles ago (about four years). What does Commission Rule 3.2 require for reinstatement?
questions.correct_answer: Renewal fee, late renewal penalty, and proof of CE from the past 24 months
distractors: Re-taking the national and state licensing exams
Automatic reinstatement upon payment of the renewal fee alone
questions.explanation: Rule 3.2(a): a license expired for less than five years is reinstated by paying the renewal fee and the late renewal penalty and providing proof of the required continuing and/or post-licensure education taken within the previous 24 months. Four years is inside that window, so no re-examination is required. Late penalties escalate under 3 V.S.A. § 127.

questions.question_text: What is the fee for the initial Vermont real estate license application?
questions.explanation: The initial application fee for a Vermont real estate license is $100 for both salespersons and brokers. The state licensure examination fee is $110, and the biennial renewal fee is $220.
